Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency / 5xx spike — urgent

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and ~8% 500 error rate on checkout calls to your Dedicated pool at ~08:45 PST. Our metrics show reserved throughput dropping below the committed QPS and requests getting queued (~120s tail latency spikes). This is affecting ~20% of our transactions and causing failed checkout attempts.

Attached: error_samples.log (small sample of 5xx traces).

Can you confirm what caused the reserved-capacity shortfall and what immediate mitigations you can apply? We need a 30–60 minute plan and a contact for an operations bridge.

This is blocking our day-of-week peak. Please escalate — we can open a bridge if needed.

Thanks,
Ashley Reed
Site Reliability Lead
FencePost Payments

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share the full trace IDs for 3 representative failures and approximate request timestamps (we have a partial sample in your attachment).

- Activate automatic fallback routing to a compatible quantized model variant (faster exec time, reduced headroom).
- Apply a short-lived rate advisory to non-critical endpoints to protect checkout flows.

On Sat, Nov 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM ops@fencepostpay.com wrote:
> We started seeing a sustained latency increase and ~8% 500 error rate on checkout calls...

Quick technical readout from infra ops so far:
- Reserved pool utilization for FencePost at peak: 98% (sustained for ~14m).
- KV cache pressure & eviction rate spiked — observed increased cache miss amplification for long-tail sessions.
- Batch window: a downstream ingestion job from a partner started a fanout; this increased concurrent sequence lengths and per-request token work.

Immediate recommendations executed: 
1) Applied a conservative autoscale permit for +2 burst nodes (temporary).
2) Flushed a small subset of the longest-lived per-tenant KV caches to recover headroom.
3) Rolled a canary routing rule to fall back to quantized-xxs model for non-critical metadata endpoints.

Attachment: pool-metrics-28nov.png (summary graphs).

Notes: the fallback reduces latency but may alter subtle output tokens for generative steps. Need customer sign-off if fallback touches business-critical inference paths (checkout risk).

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — urgent

Summary of engineering actions taken and next steps:
- Enabled emergency autoscaling policy for FencePost: +4 burst instances queued; two are live and accepting traffic.
- Activated routing fallback to quantized-xxs for 40% of background calls (non-critical) and 100% for telemetry endpoints.
- Background queue drain job started; we estimate backlog will be cleared in ~45 minutes at current drain rate.

Caveats and asks:
- Fallback will increase per-token inference divergence for ~1% of requests; recommend explicit customer opt-in for any checkout-affecting endpoints. We have a DocuSign approval link for the degraded-output fallback policy: https://docusign.example/df4821
- We will keep the burst nodes for up to 6 hours while we monitor headroom; billing/credits are negotiable.

Attached: none (see MAP-draft.pdf).

—David Kim

Hi Ashley / FencePost team,

Quick executive summary and formal next steps after our bridge: 
- Root cause (interim): sudden fanout from partner ingestion increased average sequence work and kicked the Dedicated pool above committed headroom (98% util). KV cache eviction amplified tail latency.
- Immediate mitigations applied: emergency autoscaling (+4 burst nodes), selective KV trim, routing fallback to quantized variant for non-checkout paths, backlog drain job.
- Current status: tail-latency and 5xx rate are down to baseline (~1.2% 5xx across all checkout traffic), checkout success rate restored to normal for 94% of requests. We continue to monitor.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) FencePost: confirm whether partner batch was expected or provide ingress id/time window (Owner: Ashley) — ETA: 2h.
2) Redwood Eng: finalize canary rollback / permanent routing rule for quantized variant, and gated opt-in for checkout endpoints (Owner: David) — ETA: 24h.
3) Redwood Sales/Escalations: offer a one-week credit for burst usage and a post-incident review meeting (Owner: Marissa) — ETA: 48h.

Links and artifacts: dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/overview?acct=fencepost (monitoring snapshot), HubSpot: HUB-7894, DocuSign: https://docusign.example/df4821

I'll coordinate the post-incident RCA and invite the appropriate stakeholders. Thanks everyone for fast responses on the bridge.

—Karthik
